title: Login and password reset handlers with a slog redactor
name: Auth handler logging

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps sensitive data out of its logs? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A request arrives with the header 'Authorization: Bearer abc123'. What does the request log entry contain for headers.Authorization?
choices: [REDACTED], because redactAttr lowercases each key before looking it up and is also called for attributes inside the headers group.
Bearer abc123, because redaction only applies to top-level attributes, not to grouped ones.
Bearer [REDACTED], because the redactor masks only the credential part of string values.
Nothing: attributes inside a slog.Group are never written by the JSON handler.

questions.prompt: With the debug level enabled, a client posts a login with email 'Ana@corp.example'. What appears in the 'login attempt' log line's request field?
choices: The full JSON object including the password field, because slog.Any marshals structs.
The string [REDACTED], because the key 'request' is treated as sensitive.
Only the email, masked by redactAttr, because LoginRequest.LogValue returns a group with just the email and the attribute is resolved before ReplaceAttr runs.
An empty group, because LogValue returns only the keys listed in sensitiveKeys.

questions.prompt: A developer later adds slog.String("refresh_token", tok) to the 'login succeeded' log call. What is written for that attribute?
choices: [REDACTED], because the key contains the substring 'token'.
[REDACTED], because the value looks like a JWT.
A masked value, because string values longer than 8 characters are truncated.
The raw token value, because redactAttr matches only exact lower-cased keys and 'refresh_token' is not in the list.
